items.title: Anthropic has nearly stopped hiring junior staff because AI agents now work six times as many hours
items.summary: Anthropic is hiring fewer and fewer junior staff in technical roles. The share of junior positions among new hires dropped from 27 to 9 percent since early 2025. By August 2026, AI agents across the company were already logging six times as many hours as humans. items.title: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft without any human help
items.summary: Four AI agents running on Google's Gemini 4 Argon have beaten Minecraft for the first time without human help, slaying the Ender Dragon in a fully autonomous run. With no predefined roles or strategies, they coordinated on their own, wrote 2,783 programs, exchanged 229 chat messages, and died 605 times. The session cost $1,620. The article Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft without any human help appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Two German courts now hold Google liable for what its AI overviews say
items.summary: Google tried to overturn a landmark Munich ruling on AI search liability by appealing, then quietly settled. The strategy isn't working. The Aachen Regional Court just applied the exact same reasoning in a new case where Google's AI falsely attributed criminal offenses to a doctor that actually involved someone else. items.title: Anthropic consults law firms to set fair negotiation norms before AI agents start cutting deals
items.summary: Anthropic is consulting with law firms to develop negotiation norms for AI agents that would haggle over prices, resolve complaints, or improve contracts on behalf of users. The company is also hiring lawyers and humanities scholars as "Conceptual Reasoning Fellows" to improve Claude in areas where reliable training data is scarce. items.title: AI agents have bad taste in long-term decisions and a new benchmark proves it
items.summary: A new benchmark called Taste-Bench tests how well AI agents make strategic choices during long-running tasks. Even the best model, GPT-5.6 Sol, picks the right path on just under 60 percent of simple binary questions. Thinking longer doesn't help. The article AI agents have bad taste in long-term decisions and a new benchmark proves it appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: AI agents chasing a $465 train refund invented excuses, leaked medical data, and spammed an MP's office
items.summary: Six AI agents were tasked with recovering £350 (about $465) for a canceled train ticket in an experiment. They resorted to invented excuses, lawsuit threats, and sharing confidential health data. One agent sent 187 messages in 15 days, including 50 to a British MP's office. items.title: An OpenAI model hacked a government site, grabbed 24 years of hospital data and kept it quiet
items.summary: OpenAI has published four new cases where its AI models bypassed security boundaries on their own during training or testing. In one case, a model extracted server passwords from a government website, forged authorization tokens, and downloaded 24 years of hospital data without mentioning the unauthorized access. The article An OpenAI model hacked a government site, grabbed 24 years of hospital data and kept it quiet appeared first on The Decoder

items.title: Anthropics' Claude cracks a 25-year-old NSA cryptography mystery in under 30 minutes
items.summary: Anthropic's AI model Claude has solved a 25-year-old cryptography puzzle. The mysterious seeds behind NIST's standard curves for digital signatures were provided by the NSA without explanation, raising long-standing suspicion about built-in backdoors. items.title: Deepseek V4.1 Flash 1017 beats larger rivals in agentic tasks while once again massively cutting per-task costs
items.summary: Deepseek has released V4.1-Flash-1017 as an open-weight model that posts better benchmarks, finishes tasks faster, and produces shorter outputs than its predecessor. The company is also opening up its internal search engine through new Search and Fetch APIs at $0.75 per 1,000 calls. API users in tools like Claude Code and Codex get free access for now. items.title: AI models hide mistakes in their own work reports, but one sentence in your prompt can help
items.summary: AI agents systematically skip errors in their own reports, even when they spot the problems. In a study by Google Research, MIT, and Harvard, GPT-5.5 left out negative results in 198 out of 200 paper abstracts. The article AI models hide mistakes in their own work reports, but one sentence in your prompt can help appeared first on The Decoder.
